description: The official constitution of the Actuarial Science Association of the University of Dar es Salaam (ASAUD). This document outlines the rules, governance, and operations of the association.

chapters.title: Name, Motto and Objectives
sections: The association shall be known as the Actuarial Science Association of the University of Dar es Salaam (ASAUD).
The motto of the association shall be 'Shaping the Future of Actuarial Science'.
The objectives of the association are to support actuarial students academically, professionally, and socially.

chapters.title: Membership
sections: Membership is open to all registered students of the University of Dar es Salaam.
Full membership is granted to students enrolled in the Actuarial Science programme.
Associate membership is available to students from related disciplines.
All members must abide by the constitution and code of conduct of the association.

chapters.title: Leadership and Governance
sections: The association shall be led by an Executive Committee elected annually.
The Executive Committee shall consist of the President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer, and other elected officials.
Leadership terms shall run for one academic year, renewable once.
Elections shall be held at the end of each academic year in accordance with electoral guidelines.

chapters.title: Meetings
sections: General meetings shall be held at least twice per semester.
Executive Committee meetings shall be held monthly.
Special meetings may be convened by the President or by request of at least 10 members.
Quorum for general meetings shall be 25% of active members.

chapters.title: Financial Matters
sections: The Treasurer shall manage all financial affairs of the association.
All expenditures must be approved by the Executive Committee.
Financial records shall be audited annually and presented to members.
Membership fees, if any, shall be determined by the Executive Committee.

chapters.title: Decision-Making Procedures
sections: Decisions shall be made by consensus where possible.
Where consensus cannot be reached, decisions shall be made by simple majority vote.
Constitutional amendments require a two-thirds majority of members present.
The Executive Committee has authority to make operational decisions.

chapters.title: Amendments
sections: Any member may propose amendments to the constitution in writing to the Secretary.
Proposed amendments must be circulated to members at least 14 days before voting.
Amendments require approval by two-thirds of members present at a general meeting.
Approved amendments take effect immediately upon ratification.
